summary: Session 4 of 4 (FINAL): the two things concurrent session sets collide on are gone. (1) THE APPEND-ONLY FILE. `CHANGELOG.md` was edited by every session at the same offset -- the top -- so two developers in separate worktrees were GUARANTEED a conflict, and of the worst kind: both sides correct, so resolving it is manual reading rather than a rule. Not hypothetical: 79 commits touched `ai_router/CHANGELOG.md` in 60 days. Sessions now write `changelog.d/<order>-<slug>.md`, one file per contribution -- a new file is a shape git merges cleanly -- and `python -m ai_router.changelog render` concatenates preamble + pending lead + fragments + released history on demand; `fold` writes the view back and clears the fragments at release time (operator only). This is less a new convention than an existing one made executable: the router changelog already carried NINE stacked `## [Unreleased] - ... (Set NNN)` sections and the extension's ten `###` blocks, so sessions were already partitioning by hand, inside one file, which is exactly what conflicts. THE PARTITION DOES NOT REWRITE HISTORY, AND THAT IS ENFORCED: a fragment stores the VERBATIM slice, so concatenation equals the original by construction; `.baseline.json` freezes the pre-partition digest, each fragment's digest and the fragment ORDER; `check` re-renders from the baseline set alone so a later contribution cannot make it vacuous; `restamp` covers a deliberate edit to frozen prose and REFUSES if any fragment moved. Verified against `git show HEAD:` -- render() reproduces both pre-session changelogs exactly (306,974 and 237,977 chars, LF-normalized because core.autocrlf=true would otherwise make the digest a platform assertion rather than a content one). (2) THE SET NUMBER. Verdict 6.4 asks developers to reserve numbers in chat; nothing enforced it, and the collision is invisible inside one worktree -- two branches each mint `123-` and the clash only exists after they merge. `start_session` now refuses before the work starts (scoped to THAT set's number, so an unrelated collision elsewhere does not block unrelated work), `resolve_set --check` sweeps and exits 3, and `drift_guard.py` runs both that sweep and the changelog round trip in CI's fast gate -- the right home, because both defects are introduced by a MERGE. `ai_router.modules create` deliberately gained NO check: it mints max(existing)+1 from a live listing, so a refusal there could only ever pass (L-112-1), and the property is asserted by a test instead.

residuals.source: Operator-reported during this session, 2026-08-13, after a screenshot of a duplicated `Close out` step row in the Work Explorer
residuals.description: Every staged rebuild of the extension carries the SAME version string. `package.json` has been pinned at `0.51.0` since Set 114 S3 because the operator deferred the release, so a locally rebuilt VSIX is indistinguishable from an older one to both VS Code and the developer, and installing a newer build over an older one of the same version is a no-op without `--force`. The operator lost a debugging cycle to this: they installed 'the latest VSIX', restarted, and were still running a bundle 5,076 bytes different from the tree (sha256 ED3BA3E9... vs E2817EB9...). A `--force` reinstall of a freshly packaged VSIX replaced it and made the two byte-identical.
residuals.rationale: Diagnosed and worked around here, deliberately not fixed here. The fix is a release-process change -- a build-metadata suffix on staged builds, or bumping at stage time rather than at publish -- and the version number is part of the release contract the operator owns (the 2026-08-11 ruling is that the next Marketplace push is a SINGLE folded release at a version the release-cutter assigns). Bumping it inside this session would also have re-armed L-064-12 and invalidated the full Layer 3 run that was executing at that moment. `--force` is the correct interim workaround and costs nothing.
residuals.owner: operator (release walk, with the version-assignment decision)
residuals.owner_rationale: Version assignment and publishing are operator-only authority, and this is a change to how staged builds are numbered rather than a defect in any shipped code path.

residuals.source: Operator-reported 2026-08-13 with a screenshot; not reproduced
residuals.description: The operator observed TWO `Close out` rows under Set 122 Session 4 in the Work Explorer with only that session expanded; the tooltip on one read `planned - not started` / `Close-out.`, which is session 4's seeded plan row. NOT REPRODUCIBLE from this source tree. The extension's own `buildStepRows`, run via ts-node against the real on-disk `activity-log.json` / `session-state.json` / `spec.md`, returns exactly 7 rows with ONE `close-out`; a sweep of every session of every set in the repo through the Python mirror returns `0 session(s) with duplicate step labels`; session 4's ledger holds exactly one `close-out` entry; and `git worktree list` shows no sibling roots the Explorer could be merging.
residuals.rationale: Cannot be closed without one observation that could not be taken during the session: reloading the VS Code window would have terminated the orchestrator mid-close-out. The operator was confirmed to be running a stale bundle (S122-S4-R1), which is the leading explanation, and a fresh VSIX built from this tree was force-installed and verified byte-identical to the repo bundle -- so the next window reload is the test. If the duplicate is gone it was the stale bundle and this closes; if it survives it is a live reconciliation defect and the evidence above narrows it sharply. Recorded rather than assumed-fixed, because 'I could not reproduce it' is not 'it does not happen'.
residuals.owner: operator (one window reload), then whoever next touches the Work Explorer step rows if it survives
residuals.owner_rationale: The remaining step is an observation only the operator can make, on their own VS Code window, and it takes seconds.

residuals.source: Carried in from Session 2's disposition; unchanged by this session
residuals.description: Nothing in the automated suite asserts that the PUBLISHED `dabbler-ai-router` wheel is compatible with the shipping extension. The pre-release lanes install THIS checkout via the harness-only `DABBLER_ROUTER_INSTALL_SPEC` override, because a wheel cannot contain code that has not been published yet.
residuals.rationale: Untouched by Session 4, which is router/docs-side only. Session 3 made the check EXECUTABLE and gave it one source of truth; what remains is the half only the operator can run, because it depends on an act only the operator performs. The set's spec mandates the ordering -- publish `dabbler-ai-router` first, CONFIRM THE WHEEL IS LIVE, then publish the extension -- and the post-publish step is one command: create a throwaway venv, `pip install dabbler-ai-router` from the real registry, and run `ROUTER_CAPABILITY_PROBE_CODE` against it. If that import fails, the extension must not be published.
residuals.owner: operator (release walk, immediately after this set lands)
residuals.owner_rationale: Publishing is operator-only authority in every case, and this is the one assertion that can only be made once the wheel exists. It protects every existing project taking the Marketplace update.

residuals.source: Carried in from Session 2; re-observed twice this session, now with a clean A/B on one tree
residuals.description: Layer 3 is worker-count sensitive on this hardware. This session produced the sharpest evidence yet: the SAME tree ran 29 passed / 2 failed at the local default of 4 workers and 31/31 at 2 workers, the count CI uses. One of the two 4-worker failures was a genuine regression, but `vsix-first-run-walkthrough` timed out waiting for `Default 2 sets` at 4 workers and passed in 1.6m at 2.
residuals.rationale: Not re-litigated here, but this session moves it from 'intermittent' to 'reproducible by worker count' on one tree, which is what a fix would need. Still worth deciding whether `playwright.config.ts`'s local default should simply match CI's 2 rather than 4 -- the current default costs a false failure and a full re-run on every session that trusts it.
residuals.owner_rationale: Belongs with whoever next revisits Layer 3 runtime/parallelism; the Step 9 review should decide whether lowering the local default earns its own change.

residuals.source: Observed while logging this session's own steps
residuals.description: Two of this session's logged step keys drifted from the keys `start_session` seeded from `spec.md` (`keep-the-concatenated-view-byte` vs `keep-the-concatenated-view-byte-identical`; `refuse-a-duplicate-set-number` vs `refuse-a-duplicate-set-number-at`). They reconcile correctly today only through the ORDINAL pass, which `plan_matches_spec` disables the moment the seeded plan and `spec.md` disagree -- at which point both would render as duplicate rows appended after the plan.
residuals.rationale: Harmless on this set: the plan still matches the spec, and the rendered checklist is correct in both the CLI and the tree. Fixing it after the fact would mean hand-editing a sanctioned writer's ledger, which is the mixed-mode drift the constitution forbids. Recorded because it is the nearest known mechanism to the phantom row in S122-S4-R2, and because the safe remedy is a habit rather than a patch: log a step with the key `session_checklist` already seeded, not one derived independently from the same sentence.
residuals.owner_rationale: A convention worth raising at the Step 9 review; no code change is obviously correct, since the ordinal fallback exists precisely to tolerate this.
